trajectory.patch:
The Kconfig warning indicates that `CONFIG_STDOUT_CONSOLE` cannot be enabled because its dependency `(!(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC))` evaluates to `n`. This implies that both `NATIVE_LIBRARY` and `EXTERNAL_LIBC` are `y`.

For an embedded board like `nrf52840dk_nrf52840`, `NATIVE_LIBRARY` should typically be `n`. If `NATIVE_LIBRARY` is `y`, it suggests the build environment is incorrectly treating the target as a native host library. When `NATIVE_LIBRARY` is `y`, `NATIVE_BUILD` is also `y`. In `lib/libc/Kconfig`, if `NATIVE_BUILD` is `y` and `NATIVE_LIBC_INCOMPATIBLE` is `n`, then `EXTERNAL_LIBC` becomes the default C library implementation. This chain of selections leads to `NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC` being true, thus disabling `STDOUT_CONSOLE`.

Since `CONFIG_STDOUT_CONSOLE=y` is explicitly set in `prj.conf` (which is part of the test specification and cannot be changed), and `NATIVE_LIBRARY` is implicitly `y` (as per the error log, and cannot be directly unset without knowing its source), the solution is to ensure `EXTERNAL_LIBC` is `n`. This can be achieved by selecting `NATIVE_LIBC_INCOMPATIBLE` when an embedded C library (like Picolibc or Newlib) is chosen. By doing so, `EXTERNAL_LIBC` will no longer be the default even if `NATIVE_BUILD` is `y`, forcing an embedded libc and making `EXTERNAL_LIBC` `n`. This satisfies the `STDOUT_CONSOLE` dependency `(!(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC))` (as `!(y && n)` is `y`).

This fix modifies the core `lib/libc/Kconfig` to correctly handle scenarios where `NATIVE_BUILD` might be inadvertently enabled for embedded targets, ensuring that the appropriate embedded C library is selected and `STDOUT_CONSOLE` can function as intended. The runtime assertion failure might be a consequence of this underlying configuration issue, and resolving the Kconfig warning may also resolve the crash.
